deep.reconstruction:
There are no derivations on this page. It is a hand-written table of geographic coordinates in degrees.minutes.seconds, for about 33 places in northern and central Europe plus Tobolsk.

Layout:
- Each line gives place, latitude N, then longitude E.
- The left column is sorted by decreasing latitude, from Archangel 64°34' down to Dresden 51°6'. The list continues on the next page (Erfurt, Breslau, Jena, Cöln, Prag, Frankfurt).
- A second short column (Tobolsk 58°12'30", 86°5'0"; Edinburg 55°58'0", 14°34'45") was squeezed in at the upper right.
- The sheet is a blank leaf bound into a printed elementary algebra textbook (§178, linear word problems). The previous leaf repeats the place names in its margin.

Which meridian (my inference): longitudes are counted east of Ferro (Hierro). Greenwich is listed at 17°41' and Leipzig at exactly 30°0'0". Ferro lies 17°40' west of Greenwich (20° west of Paris by convention), so Greenwich ≈ 17°40', Göttingen ≈ 27°36', Leipzig ≈ 30°02'. These agree with the table to within minutes.

Purpose: this is a reference list of positions, presumably copied from an almanac or geography (Berlin Jahrbuch / Bode type). It could serve for map work, longitude differences or great-circle distances. No such computation appears on the page.

Spot checks against modern values (my own):
- Close agreement: Petersburg 59°56'/47°59', Upsala, Stockholm, Hannover 52°22'/27°24', Oxford 51°45'/16°25', Antwerp 51°13'/22°04', Warsaw 52°14'/38°41'.
- Göttingen 51°31'54" is the pre-Gauss value from the Tobias Mayer era. Gauss's own later determination was about 51°31'48". This suggests the list predates Gauss's observatory work, or was simply copied.

The next page switches to Gauss's study of the Euler-type integral ∫x^m dx/(1+x^n)^{p/n}, so this leaf is a mere memorandum.
errors: Leiden longitude 44°18'45" is impossible. The correct value is about 22°09' east of Ferro (4°29' east of Greenwich), so this is a copying slip; the latitude 52°8'40" is fine.
Dublin latitude 52°12' is wrong; the true value is about 53°21'. The entry is therefore misplaced in the latitude-sorted order. Its longitude 10°49'45" is also about 35' off (true ≈ 11°24').
Greifswald: latitude 54°14'40" is about 9' too high (true 54°05'). Longitude 33°10'30" is about 2° too large (true ≈ 31°03').
Kiel longitude 28°53' is about 1° too large (true ≈ 27°48'). Königsberg 39°17'30" is also about 1° too large (true ≈ 38°10').
Archangel longitude 56°35' is about 1.6° too small (true ≈ 58°12'). Moscow 55°36' is about 20' too large. Both reflect older 18th-century determinations.
Halle latitude 51°34' (true 51°29') and Hamburg latitude 53°36' (true 53°33') are slightly off, consistent with the 18th-century tables they were taken from.

results.what: Table of latitudes and longitudes (east of Ferro) of European cities, sorted by latitude
results.usually_credited_to: Standard 18th-century almanac data (e.g. Berliner Astronomisches Jahrbuch, Connaissance des Temps)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a copied list of geographic coordinates with no mathematics. It is routine reference material, with some copying errors and outdated 18th-century values.

checkable.asserts: Göttingen minus Greenwich longitude from the table gives 9°53' east of Greenwich. The modern value is 9°56'.
Leipzig lies 12°19' east of Greenwich by the table. The modern value is 12°22'.
The table's Leiden entry would place Leiden about 26°38' east of Greenwich, versus the true 4°29'. This confirms the copying error.
Great-circle distance Göttingen–Berlin from the table values is about 260 km (Berlin longitude read as 31°4'15"; rad means degrees to radians).

transcription_corrections: Edinburg is not a line of the main column. Together with Tobolsk it forms a separate two-line insertion at the upper right.
Berlin longitude: the minutes digit is heavily overwritten with a large '6'. The underlying reading is probably 31°4'15" (or 31°3'), not 31°6'.
Copenhagen longitude reads '30. 6. 4' with the 6 overwritten. It may be an incomplete '30°6'45"'.
